youtube.title: What If You Held Your Breath Like a GTA 6 Character? #Shorts
youtube.description:
What if you could hold your breath like a GTA 6 character? Swim to the bottom, look around, take your time. Remy runs three tests on how long a real person can hold their breath.

Test 1, on land: most adults can hold their breath for about 30 to 90 seconds. Trained freedivers practise for years to reach several minutes; the static apnea record without extra oxygen is 11:35 (over eleven minutes).
Test 2, cold water: falling into cold water makes you gasp in the first minute, whether you want to or not. Rescuers teach the 1-10-1 rule: about 1 minute to control your breathing, about 10 minutes of useful movement, around 1 hour before hypothermia takes over (a memory aid, not exact times).
Test 3, diving games: pushing a breath hold underwater can make you black out without warning (shallow water / hypoxic blackout).

That's why safety experts say: never hold your breath underwater alone, and never ignore the urge to breathe. In the game, your air bar refills at the surface. In real life, a buddy and a life jacket are your extra lives. How long can you hold your breath?

Safety: Never practise holding your breath underwater alone. Don't hyperventilate before swimming underwater, don't play breath-holding games, and always swim where a lifeguard or a buddy is watching.

Sources:
- How long people can hold their breath (untrained adults about 30-90 s, freedivers several minutes): Healthline: https://www.healthline.com/health/holding-your-breath , BBC Science Focus: https://www.sciencefocus.com/the-human-body/how-long-can-you-hold-breath
- Static apnea record without pure oxygen (AIDA), 11:35: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Static_apnea
- Cold water shock and the 1-10-1 principle: Cold Water Safety / CSBC: https://csbc.ca/1-10-1-principle/ , U.S. Army: https://www.army.mil/article/212474/tips_to_survive_a_fall_into_cold_water , Washington State Parks: https://parks.wa.gov/about/news-center/field-guide-blog/cold-water-shock-what-it-and-how-protect-yourself
- Shallow water (hypoxic) blackout: American Red Cross: https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/articles/shallow-water-hypoxic-blackout , CDC drowning prevention: https://www.cdc.gov/drowning/prevention/

Not medical or safety-training advice. Learn water safety from a qualified instructor.
